note: PR #104 split IDEAS.md (8,278 lines) by lifting §6, the agent log, into docs/agent-log.md (6,431 lines) and leaving IDEAS.md at 2,025 lines, opened by a Map of every subsection. Full suite 1103 passed; doc gate 28; ci-lint clean.

decisions.question: How do you split an 8,000-line document without it rotting into an index that lies?
decisions.commitment: As a derive-and-gate, not a move. A Map at the top of IDEAS.md lists every subsection (§1.1 through §8.3) across both files with its status and a link, and a new test (test_the_map_indexes_every_subsection_and_no_ghosts) asserts an exact bijection with the ### headings across both files AND that each row's status matches its heading. Add, rename, retag, or move a subsection without updating the Map and CI fails. The status-tag gate now scans both files.
decisions.why: The instruction was that the split be recursive — the document's own method (derive from the tree, gate it, don't assert) applied to itself. So the deliverable is not the smaller file; it is the gate that keeps the smaller file honest, the same discipline as the module-list and docs-list gates already in test_docs.

decisions.question: §6 is wired into the code by number and read by several tools. What has to hold across the move?
decisions.commitment: Every §6.N number is preserved, so 'IDEAS §6.40' in code comments and prose still resolves; only the file moved. The four §6 readers were repointed — before_write.py (the write-gate's open-finding count), review_desk.py (seeds the review desk), extract_ideas.py (now reads both files, tolerating the log's absence on pre-split refs) — and dogfood_next_piece.py uses a hardcoded list, unaffected. The 13 relative links inside the moved content were repointed for the docs/ base and re-verified.
decisions.why: A split that broke the citations or the write-gate's finding-source would trade length for correctness. The numbers are the contract the rest of the tree cites against, so preserving them is the whole point of moving rather than renumbering.
